- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent history, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid premature reversal.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast slope or add a dampening factor.  
- Model consistently underestimates long-term upward trends (especially >10-day horizons) — apply a small upward bias (e.g., +1–2% of recent mean) for 30-day forecasts.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion — add a slight downward bias to prevent over-optimism.  
- Model tends to lag in recognizing true turning points — especially when sentiment is low — delay forecast adjustment until 2–3 days after sentiment shifts.
